html:
The Bosnian crisis began on 6 October 1908 when Austria Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, which it had occupied and run since the Congress of Berlin in 1878 while it formally stayed Ottoman.

Under Austrian rule Bosnia got railways, mines, a modern Sarajevo and a new civil service, but most peasants stayed bound to Muslim landlords. The annexation enraged Serbia, which hoped to unite the South Slavs, and Russia, which was forced to back down when Germany stood by Austria. The crisis hardened the alliances and set young Bosnian Serb radicals against Austria. Six years later one of them shot the Austrian heir in Sarajevo in the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
sum: The Bosnian crisis began on 6 October 1908 when Austria Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, which it had occupied and run since the Congress of Berlin in 1878 while it formally stayed Ottoman.
